column4: Set up CI pipeline for tests and Docker build
column6:
h3. User story / objective

Technical objective: every push and pull request is tested automatically so that main stays releasable.

h3. Description

There is no CI configuration in the repository (no .github/workflows). Add a GitHub Actions workflow that installs requirements-dev.txt with constraints.txt, runs pytest on Python 3.11 (minimum supported) and 3.13, and runs the opt-in Docker deployment test (CAG_TEST_DOCKER=1 pytest -k docker) on Linux.

h3. Business / technical value

Prevents regressions from reaching main; the documented Python minimum (3.11) is currently untested.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Workflow runs on push and on pull requests to main
* Test job runs on Python 3.11 and 3.13 and fails the build on any test failure
* Docker job builds the image and runs the Docker deployment test
* Branch protection on main requires the CI checks to pass (configured by a repo admin)
* README documents the CI and how to reproduce it locally

h3. Security considerations

Pin third-party actions to commit SHAs; the pipeline needs no secrets; use least-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN permissions (contents: read).

h3. Testing requirements

Open a test PR with a deliberately failing test and verify the check blocks the merge.

h3. Planning

* Backlog ref: S1.1
* Category: Remaining work
* Phase: Phase 0 - Close critical gaps now
* Story points: 3 (estimate)

column4: Introduce Alembic schema migrations with a baseline of the current schema
column6:
h3. User story / objective

Technical objective: schema changes (starting with Asset Monitoring) can be applied to existing databases without data loss.

h3. Description

Tables are created with SQLAlchemy create_all (asset_inventory, asset_tags, users, user_sessions, audit_events) and raw CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (Monitoring tables). create_all cannot alter existing tables. Add Alembic, create a baseline revision matching the current schema (including the audit_events append-only triggers and CHECK constraints) and a documented procedure to stamp existing databases.

h3. Business / technical value

Required before any column change to existing tables, e.g. linking monitoring hosts to assets (S4.2).

h3. Acceptance criteria

* alembic upgrade head on an empty database produces a schema identical to the current create_all + init_db schema (verified by comparing sqlite_master)
* Existing databases can be stamped at the baseline without changes to data
* Application startup refuses to start (clear log message) or upgrades automatically when migrations are pending - behaviour decided and documented
* Backup is recommended/created before migrations in the documented procedure
* README section 'Database initialization and migrations' is updated

h3. Dependencies

* S2.1 Review and merge login, RBAC and audit log (feature/auth-rbac-audit)

h3. Security considerations

Migrations must preserve the audit_events UPDATE/DELETE triggers.

h3. Testing requirements

Automated test: upgrade from empty DB and from a copy of a pre-migration DB; data and triggers intact.

h3. Planning

* Backlog ref: S1.2
* Category: Technical debt
* Phase: Phase 1 - Foundation and hardening
* Story points: 5 (estimate)

column4: Rate-limit login attempts per client IP
column6:
h3. User story / objective

As a security administrator, I want login attempts limited per IP address, so that password spraying across many accounts is slowed down.

h3. Description

Only per-account lockout exists (CAG_LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES). An attacker can try one password against many usernames without triggering a lockout. Add an IP-based limit for /auth/login.

h3. Business / technical value

Mitigates credential stuffing / password spraying.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* More than N failed logins per IP within a window return HTTP 429 (N and window configurable)
* Successful logins are not blocked for other IPs
* Rate-limit hits are written to the audit log (action auth.rate_limited)
* Works behind a reverse proxy when proxy headers are trusted explicitly (documented)

h3. Dependencies

* S2.1 Review and merge login, RBAC and audit log (feature/auth-rbac-audit)

h3. Security considerations

Do not trust X-Forwarded-For unless configured; avoid unbounded in-memory state.

h3. Testing requirements

Automated tests for limit, window reset, audit entry and proxy-header handling.

h3. Planning

* Backlog ref: S2.2
* Category: Remaining work
* Phase: Phase 1 - Foundation and hardening
* Story points: 3 (estimate)

column4: Force password change after administrator-set passwords

h3. User story / objective

As a user, I want to be required to choose my own password after an administrator created or reset it, so that only I know my password.

h3. Description

Administrators set initial passwords and reset passwords (POST /users, POST /users/{id}/password, maintenance create-user/reset-password). Add a must_change_password flag that restricts the session to the password-change endpoint until a new password is set.

h3. Business / technical value

Administrators no longer know users' long-term passwords.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Users created or reset by an admin/CLI must change their password at next login
* Until changed, all endpoints except /auth/me, /auth/password and /auth/logout return 403
* The UI redirects to the password-change page
* Self-service changes clear the flag; audit entries record the forced change

h3. Dependencies

* S2.1 Review and merge login, RBAC and audit log (feature/auth-rbac-audit)
* S1.2 Introduce Alembic schema migrations with a baseline of the current schema

h3. Security considerations

Flag must be enforced server-side, not only in the UI.

h3. Testing requirements

column4: Personal API tokens for automation
column6:
h3. User story / objective

As an analyst, I want a personal API token, so that scripts can use the API without my password or a browser session.

h3. Description

The API currently only accepts the session cookie. Add personal tokens (Bearer) that inherit the user's role, have an expiry, can be revoked and are shown once.

h3. Business / technical value

Enables integrations (CI, scripts, future SIEM export) without sharing passwords.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Users can create, list (without secret) and revoke their own tokens; admins can revoke any token
* Only a hash of the token is stored; the token is shown exactly once
* Tokens expire (max lifetime configurable) and stop working when the user is disabled
* Requests with a token are attributed to the user in the audit log (with token id)
* CSRF origin check is not required for token-authenticated requests and still applies to cookies

h3. Dependencies

* S2.1 Review and merge login, RBAC and audit log (feature/auth-rbac-audit)
* S1.2 Introduce Alembic schema migrations with a baseline of the current schema

h3. Security considerations

Constant-time comparison, token prefix for secret scanning, never log tokens.

h3. Testing requirements

API tests for lifecycle, expiry, revocation, RBAC parity with sessions and audit attribution.

h3. Planning

* Backlog ref: S2.4
* Category: Remaining work
* Phase: Phase 2 - Asset Monitoring (next development step)

column4: Audit log retention, export and archival
column6:
h3. User story / objective

As a compliance officer, I want a defined retention period and an export of the audit log, so that personal data (usernames, IP addresses) is not kept longer than necessary and evidence can be archived.

h3. Description

audit_events is append-only via database triggers and grows without limit. Define a retention period, an export (CSV/JSON) for administrators and a controlled archival/purge procedure that works with the append-only triggers.

h3. Business / technical value

GDPR data minimisation and audit evidence for reviews.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Retention period documented with its justification
* Admins can export filtered audit events (CSV and JSON); exports are themselves audit-logged
* Maintenance command archives and purges events older than the retention period, leaving an audit record of the purge
* Normal API/application code still cannot update or delete audit events

h3. Dependencies

* S2.1 Review and merge login, RBAC and audit log (feature/auth-rbac-audit)

h3. Security considerations

CSV export must neutralise formula injection; purge only through the maintenance command with explicit confirmation.

h3. Testing requirements

column4: Scan targets are passed to nmap without validation (argument injection)
column6:
h3. User story / objective

As a security administrator, I want scan targets validated before they reach nmap, so that a user cannot inject nmap options.

h3. Description

Verified in code: app/monitoring/scanner.py (lines 168-227) splits the user-supplied target on whitespace and appends the parts to the nmap argument list. A target beginning with '-' (e.g. '--script=...', '-iL /path', '-oN /path') is interpreted as an nmap option. Not exploited or tested here (nmap is not installed in the review environment). Endpoints: POST /monitoring/discover, /portscan, /versionscan, /schedules; after S2.1 only analysts/admins can call them, on current main anyone can.

h3. Business / technical value

Prevents reading/writing server files or running nmap scripts through the API.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Each target token must be a valid IPv4/IPv6 address, CIDR, nmap octet range or hostname; anything else returns 422 with a clear message
* Tokens starting with '-' are always rejected
* Port specs are validated against an allow-list pattern
* Same validation applies to stored schedules (existing invalid schedules are disabled with a log entry)

h3. Security considerations

Treat as a security bug; fix before exposing the Monitoring API to any network.

h3. Testing requirements

Unit tests with malicious targets (option injection, shell metacharacters, very long input); tests assert nmap is never invoked for rejected input.

h3. Planning

* Backlog ref: B4.1
* Category: Remaining work
* Phase: Phase 0 - Close critical gaps now
* Story points: 2 (estimate)

h3. Business / technical value

Protects the host, the database and scanned networks.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Minimum schedule interval configurable (default e.g. 15 minutes)
* limit parameters capped (e.g. 500) and validated
* Concurrent scans limited

h3. Dependencies

* B4.1 Scan targets are passed to nmap without validation (argument injection)

h3. Security considerations

Availability (DoS) protection.

h3. Testing requirements

Validation tests for boundaries.

h3. Planning

* Backlog ref: B4.2
* Category: Remaining work
* Phase: Phase 1 - Foundation and hardening
* Story points: 1 (estimate)

column4: Restrict scans to authorised network ranges
column6:
h3. User story / objective

As a security administrator, I want scans limited to approved network ranges, so that the tool cannot be used to scan third-party systems.

h3. Description

Any target accepted by nmap can be scanned today. Add a configurable allow-list (CAG_SCAN_ALLOWED_NETWORKS, default private ranges) checked after DNS resolution.

h3. Business / technical value

Legal and ethical safety: scanning without authorisation can be illegal.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Targets outside the allow-list are rejected with 403 and audit-logged
* Hostnames are resolved and every resolved address must be inside the allow-list
* CIDR/range targets must lie completely inside the allow-list
* Default and override documented

h3. Dependencies

* B4.1 Scan targets are passed to nmap without validation (argument injection)

h3. Security considerations

Resolve DNS once and pass the resolved addresses to nmap to avoid DNS rebinding.

h3. Testing requirements

Unit tests for inside/outside/partially-overlapping ranges and hostnames.

h3. Planning

* Backlog ref: S4.1
* Category: Remaining work
* Phase: Phase 0 - Close critical gaps now
* Story points: 3 (estimate)

column4: Link discovered hosts to managed assets
column6:
h3. User story / objective

As an analyst, I want hosts found by scans matched to inventory assets, so that monitoring results belong to the right asset.

h3. Description

The Monitoring 'assets' table (hosts keyed by IP) and asset_inventory (UUID) are separate; no code connects them. Add a link from discovered hosts to asset_inventory.id with automatic matching by IP/hostname and manual confirmation; unmatched hosts become 'discovered, unmanaged' candidates that an analyst can turn into assets.

h3. Business / technical value

Core of block 2: monitoring data in asset context.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Scan results of a host with a matching active asset are linked automatically (rule documented)
* Ambiguous matches are not linked automatically and are shown for manual decision
* Unmatched hosts are listed and can be converted into an asset (prefilled form)
* IP changes of an asset do not break existing links (link is by asset id)
* Linking/unlinking is audit-logged

h3. Dependencies

* S1.2 Introduce Alembic schema migrations with a baseline of the current schema
* S2.1 Review and merge login, RBAC and audit log (feature/auth-rbac-audit)
* B4.1 Scan targets are passed to nmap without validation (argument injection)

h3. Security considerations
